The dynamics of the double pendulum are governed by coupled nonlinear ODEs derived from Lagrangian mechanics:

\dot{\theta_1} = \omega_1

\dot{\theta_2} = \omega_2

\dot{\omega_1} = f_1(\theta_1, \theta_2, \omega_1, \omega_2; g, l_1, l_2, m_1, m_2)

\dot{\omega_2} = f_2(\theta_1, \theta_2, \omega_1, \omega_2; g, l_1, l_2, m_1, m_2, damping)

where f_1, f_2 involve sines, cosines, and damping terms linear in \omega.

Since all physical parameters are hidden, f_1 and f_2 cannot be evaluated. Damping and gravity torques cannot be inferred from a single initial state.

For small t = 0.01 s, use lowest-order approximation consistent with known initial conditions: treat \omega as constant (ignoring unknown \dot{\omega}), integrate \dot{\theta} = \omega.

Thus, \theta(t) \approx \theta(0) + \omega(0) t, \ \omega(t) \approx \omega(0).

\theta(0) must be measured from image.
